rules.title: One bound per plan bound (connections)
rules.rule: Seed ZZ6GMP (the only (2 seg,1 pax) seed) is a round trip with TWO JOURNEY_SERVER_BOUND itineraries; builder.walk() only rewrites their end points, so two segments of one spec bound become two Raptor bounds (observed: two APPR rows per pax, bound 2 = NE-08 'origin'/NE-27 instead of NE-12/13/18/19, and delayMin of the more delayed bound). Post-process every PNR message in scenario_build.build_one (all families): set processedPnr.flightItineraries to one JOURNEY_SERVER_BOUND per plan.bounds entry listing that bound's segment ids in order {flights:[{flightSegment:{id}}...]}, originIataCode=first.origin, destinationIataCode=last.destination (also the TK/HK replacement ids the builder appends).
rules.evidence: engine/src/booking/pnr.rs:1051-1075 (bound rph = position among JOURNEY_SERVER_BOUND itineraries, segments = all flights/connectedFlights); builder.py:538-544; facts/dds/builtins.rs destination() ~250-295: boarded seg1 + unboarded seg2 in ONE bound -> travelled_any=true, last completed arrival YYZ is a promised intermediate -> INTERMEDIATE -> NE-12/13/18/19/EL-17/18; in its own bound the unboarded seg is ORIGIN/REMAINED_AT_ORIGIN -> NE-08/09/14/15

rules.title: Rebooked passengers must check in and board the replacement flight
rules.rule: spec_to_build.py:123 skips check_in/boarding for every cancelled/rebooked segment and never emits them for the replacement (a segment index len(segs)+n). With no boarding/flown coupon Raptor reads the passenger as NO TRAVEL (ORIGIN): code EL-13 (400, band NO_TRAVEL) or NE-08, delay 0, instead of PROMISED + delay vs promise. Emit, for each accepted rebooking n (k_new = len(spec segments)+n, in rebooking-list order = builder execution order), check_in at departure:k_new -180 and boarding at departure:k_new -25 (+dep delay); for accepted:false (declined) emit nothing (no-travel is then right, delayMin = MSL own delay). Replacement FDM: kind ontime (or delay by r.arrDelayMin), arrival = rebooking arrLocal.
rules.evidence: facts/dds/builtins.rs destination(): `!travelled_any && (index==0||actual.len()==1)` -> ORIGIN; passengers.rs travelled()=boarded||flown; dds-arrival-delay.dsl: ORIGIN/INTERMEDIATE use MSL's own delay (or 0) instead of promised-vs-actual; observed FD_TC_034 EL-13 NO_TRAVEL 400 delay 0, FD_TC_031-036/237 delay 0

rules.title: Cancel code must be a NetLine 4-letter code in APPR_cancellation_lookup
rules.rule: Cancel outcomes carry the text's code into legCancelCodePrimary. Numeric IATA delay codes (31,18,96,36,62..) and invented codes (SOP, FOC, SKD, WXX) are not keys of APPR_cancellation_lookup -> msl_flight_disruption_type=OTHER -> ND-X02 / NO_DETERMINATION. Lookup keys: AIRS ARPT RUNW RTNS DAMA POLI INDU WEAT (UNCONTROLLABLE); COMM HOLI OPER POSI REPO EQUI FUEL HDLG ROTA CREW (CONTROLLABLE); PERF TECH (SAFETY). Map to a key with the expected controllability (default OPER / WEAT / TECH) and set expect.cause to that code (Raptor reports the cancellation code as cause). Exception: WXX in FD_TC_237 is intentionally OTHER (expects NO_DETERMINATION).
rules.evidence: studio-rules dds-msl-flight-disruption-type (first rows): cancellation code not_in APPR_cancellation_lookup.key -> OTHER; lookup-tables 'APPR Cancellation Code Lookup (consolidated)'; builtins.rs msl_codes(): cancellation wins over delay codes

rules.title: Rebooking chains: one step per replaced segment
rules.rule: spec_to_build emits one flight_cancelled_rebooked per rebooking entry, all with segment=k of the ORIGINAL segment. After the first, that segment is gone (builder: 'segment 1 is not in the PNR') so only the first replacement exists (FD_TC_006 saw only AC425). The builder also forces the replacement's origin/destination to the replaced segment's (builder.py step_flight_cancelled_rebooked spec dict), so ONE_TO_MANY / MANY_TO_ONE and VOL->INVOL chains are not expressible. Collapse to the final replacement per replaced segment (last INVOL entry), with the promise = the booked flight (the last VOL flight is made the booked segment), delay = final arrival - booked arrival.
rules.evidence: builder.py:976-1022; itinerary.rs Promise::bounded (promise = itinerary before first involuntary FLIGHT_REBOOKING, else the 14-day mark); bound.promised, not the rebooked flight, supplies the MSL (builtins.rs most_significant)

rules.title: INVOL schedule change: FDM delay is relative to the shifted schedule
rules.rule: scenario_build uses the Build segment's (already shifted) dep/arr for the FDM message, then adds `minutes` on top: delay is counted twice (FD_TC_009 240->480, 011 300->600, 012 270->540, 028 420->840). Set flight minutes = arrDelayMin - sum(arrDeltaMin of that segment's scheduleChanges) (depMinutes likewise with depDeltaMin), floor 0. When the remainder is 0 the code must still be sent: in scenario_fdm.py emit ARRIVAL_CODE (and the delay element) when f.codeOnly is true even if minutes==0 (or use minutes=1 as fallback, tolerance +-2).
rules.evidence: scenario_build.py segs[...].dep_utc after step_schedule_change; Flight::promised_arrival_delay() = on-block minus the PROMISED itinerary's arrival (itinerary.rs:~115); promise = 14-day mark itinerary because a retime never locks (itinerary.rs locks())

rules.title: Voluntary changes must predate the 14-day mark
rules.rule: A VOL retime/rebooking inside 14 days is invisible (builder retime keeps status HK so eds-stc-schedule-change needs TK; builder UN/TK pairs are INVOLUNTARY by eds-involuntary-change-detection step 5) and the promise stays the original (FD_TC_181-185, 104: delay 180-300 instead of 0). Emit VOL changes >= 15 days before the last original departure (noticeHours>=360 / changeDaysBeforeFlight=15): Promise::bounded then takes the itinerary at the cutoff (already changed) as the promise and deducts nothing.
rules.evidence: itinerary.rs Promise::bounded: cutoff = last original departure - 14d; `mark = at_time(cutoff)`; changes before cutoff are filtered out; without lock `snapshot = ... unwrap_or(mark)`; rules/eds-stc-schedule-change.dsl; rules/eds-involuntary-change-detection.dsl

rules.title: Formula 2 (customer's own later rebooking) cannot be built; use the net delay
rules.rule: Scenarios with INVOL rebook + VOL Pre-Move deduction (FD_TC_007, 196-200) expect the NET delay. The builder has no customer-rebooking family (HK add + old segment removed, no UN). Send the flight late by the net delay so delayMin/band/amount/code match; document history as unsupported.

rules.title: Sister-city rebooking (SISTER_PROMISED) needs a post-build patch and YTZ
rules.rule: The only sister pair near these scenarios in sister_cities_lookup is YYZ<->YTZ (YHM is NOT a sister city of YYZ, so YUL->YHM rebookings read OTHER/INTERMEDIATE). The builder forces the replacement's destination to the original's. For FD_TC_031/032/033/036/040/041/042 post-process in scenario_build: after the build, in every PNR version set the replacement product's airSegment.arrival.iataCode='YTZ' (and the FDM extra flight destination YTZ). Then bound_destination_type=SISTER_PROMISED -> EL-04/05/06 (10/11/12 with fallback).
rules.evidence: builtins.rs destination(): same_or_sister(arrival, promised_destination) -> SISTER_PROMISED; lookup-tables 'Sister Cities' (YYZ:[YTZ]); appr-compensation-eligible-reason.dsl EL-04..06,10..12

rules.title: No-travel delayMin is the MSL's own delay
rules.rule: For ORIGIN/SISTER_ORIGIN/INTERMEDIATE the reported arrival_delay_in_minutes = MSL flight's own arrival delay (else departure delay, else 0), NOT promised-vs-actual; a cancelled MSL has 0 (eligibility via msl_no_travel_delay_qualifies = cancelled || delay>=180). So expected delayMin>0 for cancelled/no-travel cases (FD_TC_047,048,088,142,160,161,237) is reachable only for a PROMISED/travelled passenger (R2) and delayMin of a cancelled no-travel is 0: set expect.delayMin null/0 for those.
